hints: Look carefully at what each dashed line touches. J is on the y-axis at the flat plateau, while K and M are on the x-axis at very different positions on the curve.
Recall the definition of Km as the substrate concentration that gives half of Vmax, so you need both a rate value that is half the maximum and its matching substrate concentration.
walkthrough:
**Find Vmax on the curve**

Think of the curve in two parts. The steep rise is when more substrate means faster rate. The flat plateau is when all active sites are full.

That plateau rate is Vmax, and point J marks it on the y-axis:
$$V_{max} = J$$

**Find half Vmax**

Km is defined very simply. It is the substrate concentration that gives half the maximum rate.

So first we need the rate value:
$$\text{rate for Km} = \frac{V_{max}}{2}$$
Point L marks this half-maximum rate on the y-axis.

**Read off Km on the x-axis**

Now go across from that half rate to the curve, then straight down to the x-axis. That substrate concentration is Km.

Point K marks exactly that substrate concentration. So L gives you the correct rate, and K gives you the correct concentration. Together they give Km.

options.A: J is Vmax, but K on its own does not tell you it is the half-Vmax concentration unless you also have L to confirm the rate.
options.B: J is Vmax and M is the substrate concentration for full saturation, not for half Vmax, so this cannot give Km.
options.C: L is half Vmax on the y-axis and K is its matching substrate concentration on the x-axis, which is exactly the definition of Km.
options.D: L is the correct half rate, but M is the saturating substrate concentration at Vmax, not the concentration at half Vmax.
